title: What is known about 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1LA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1LA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is always an alternating block (10)^x next to a solid block 1^y, and the machine moves cells between them by doubling, like its near-twin 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; an exact macro simulator finds no halt in the first 1015 steps. Lean proves both phase rules (below) for all sizes.

What Lean proves. The whole phase map, every case for all sizes (E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t), and halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from A(0, 0) (the blank tape), reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By native_decide the first 108 phases (about 4.1·1021 machine steps) do not. Lean also proves that the even phases lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape, and checks, for every all-ones tape of length n < 105, that its run halts before the next even phase or all-ones tape exactly when n is 3 or 28·2k − 2k − 13 (15, 41, 95, 205, …). What is not proved: that this list holds for every n, and that the run never lands on it.

Where a halt would come from. F0 halts, and F is entered only from E0: the machine halts only when E stands at the left end with at most one 1 after the alternating block. Probing every two-block tape with x, y < 150, a parity rule keeps that from happening except right after the tape has become all ones; from 1^n A>0 it halts exactly for n = 3, 15, 29, 41, 95, 205 (n ≤ 400), the list n = 28·2k − 2k − 13 plus 3 and 29.

Why it has not halted. All-ones moments are rare: in the first 109 steps the tape was 1^n A>0 at n = 4, 10, 58, 81, 278 and 634, and between 109 and 1015 steps only at n = 5881, 9702, 12113, 28074, 29561 and 405562. None is in the list. The machine very probably never halts, but nothing here proves it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,094 cells have been visited and 3,056 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.343).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: The exact macro simulator c/mrun.c (blocks of 2 cells, run-length coded, a run crossed at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with) runs 1015 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The two phase rules, along the run
claims.text: Write E(x,z) for E>0 (10)^x 1^z and A(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y A>0 (blank around). In the first 109 steps every left phase with z ≥ 2x+8 went E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) (469 times) and every right phase with y even and 2x ≥ y+8 went A(x,y) → A(x−y/2−2, 2y+6) (495 times).

claims.title: The two phase rules, for all sizes
claims.text: Lean proves, with rfl steps, the crossing lemmas and induction on the number of bounces, that E(x,z) reaches E(2x+4, z−2x−6) whenever x ≥ 1 and z ≥ 2x + 7 (ephase), and A(x,y) reaches A(x−y/2−2, 2y+6) whenever y ≥ 4 is even and 2x ≥ y + 4 (aphase). Each phase is a start piece, one bounce (10)^(m+1) 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^(r+3) to (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^(j+1) 1^(r+1) per copy of 10, and an end piece, generated by py/gen_rules.py; the proof is the one of 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE, with a different start piece for the A phase. The parity analysis that uses these rules is not proved.

claims.title: Step counts of the phases
claims.text: From probes: the left phase takes 4x²+24x+30 steps (the same as in its twin, whose states D, E, F, B it shares) and the right phase y²+6y+12. Doubling costs the square of the block, so the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>.

claims.title: Halting needs an all-ones tape from a sparse list
claims.text: From every two-block tape with x, y, z < 150 the next one was computed. E(x,z) with z even ≥ 2 and A(x,y) with x ≥ 1, y even lead only to tapes of the same kind or to an all-ones tape 1^n A>0, never to a halt; the machine halts only from E(x,0) and E(x,1). From 1^n A>0 the next tape is E(3, n−2), the alternating block then goes 3, 10, 24, 52, … (x ↦ 2x+4), and the run halts exactly when the ones run out leaving one: n = 15, 41, 95, 205, … = 28·2k − 2k − 13, plus 3 and 29 (all n ≤ 400 checked directly). Not proved for all sizes.

claims.title: All-ones moments so far
claims.text: In the first 109 steps the tape is 1^n A>0 at n = 4, 10, 58, 81, 278, 634 (the last at step 3,956,315). Between 109 and 1015 steps, from the exact macro simulation (which sees the moment 1^(n+1) <C two steps later): n = 5881, 9702, 12113, 28074, 29561, 405562, at steps about 2.93·109, 1.28·1010, 2.48·1010, 3.10·1011, 3.62·1011 and 9.26·1014. None is in the list (its members near them: 7139, 14305, 28639, 229337, 458711).

claims.title: The whole phase map
claims.text: Write E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t. next sends each of them to the next one the machine reaches (bounces taken all at once), with 25 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters (one symbolic run of lean/Pieces.lean each, generated by py/pieces.py, and induction for the bounces). next fails only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), which halt (e_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1)
claims.text: halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from A(0, 0) (the blank tape) is E(x, z) with z ≤ 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined and none is E(x, 0) or E(x, 1). By the step counts of the pieces (py/phasemap.py run) that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps.

claims.title: The parity classes
claims.text: even_next: the even phases (E(x, z) with z even and z ≥ 2, A(x, y) with x ≥ 1 and y even, Q(m, j, t) with t even) lead only to even phases or to an all-ones tape. So from an even phase the machine cannot halt before the tape is next all ones (even_safe).

claims.title: The fatal all-ones lengths below 10<sup>5</sup>
claims.text: fatal_list, by native_decide: for every n < 105, the run from the all-ones tape A(0, n) reaches a halting phase before an even phase or another all-ones tape exactly when n is 3 or 28·2k − 2k − 13 (15, 41, 95, 205, …) (ones_fatal, ones_safe). That the list goes on this way for every n is not proved.

claims.title: All-ones moments in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: Iterating the map with the pieces' step counts (py/phasemap.py run 100000000): after n = 405562 (step 9.26·1014) the tape is all ones at n = 2163590, 2453178, 10123514, 11319782 and 23880729 (the last near step 1.89·1020). None is fatal.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It would need an all-ones tape whose length is in a sparse list; nothing rules that out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the mechanism is clear. The tape is an alternating block next to a solid block; the machine doubles one at the other's expense, back and forth. It can halt only right after the tape becomes all ones, and only if the number of ones is in a sparse list (15, 41, 95, 205, …).

facts.text: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases of the phase map proved in Lean (about 4.1·10<sup>21</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the phase map, iterated from the start, reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1).
No halt in an exact macro simulation (blocks of 2 cells, runs crossed at once).
The tape is an alternating block and a solid block; each phase doubles one of them.
From an all-ones tape it halts exactly for n = 3, 15, 29, 41, 95, 205 (checked to n = 400).
E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) and A(x,y) → A(x−y/2−2, 2y+6), proved in Lean for all sizes.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,094 cells visited.

sections.heading: Two blocks, doubling
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell and the tape is always an alternating block 10 10 10 … followed by a solid block of 1s. With a for 10, around step 4.8·107:

At the right end the solid block doubles (226, 458, 922), eating the alternating block; when that no longer fits the head goes to the left end and the alternating block doubles instead (291 to 582), eating the solid one. Writing E(x,z) for E>0 (10)^x 1^z and A(x,y) for (10)^x 1^y A>0:

• left phase: E(x,z) → E(2x+4, z−2x−6) while z ≥ 2x+8, in 4x²+24x+30 steps: the head bounces between the blocks, each bounce moving one 10 across and turning two 1s into another 10;
  • right phase: A(x,y) → A(x−y/2−2, 2y+6) for even y while it fits, in y²+6y+12 steps.

Each doubling of a block of size x costs about x² steps, and the tape grows by a few cells per phase change, so a tape of width w takes about w³ steps: the width grows like the cube root of time. The split between the blocks moves like the doubling map x ↦ 2x on a circle, a textbook chaotic map.

sections.heading: Halting needs an exact landing
html: F reading 0 halts, and F is entered only from E reading 0; E and F together walk right over 0101…. So the run halts only from E>0 (10)^x or E>0 (10)^x 1: a left phase that uses up the solid block leaving exactly one 1.

Parity prevents that in the normal course of things: probing all two-block tapes with sizes below 150, if z is even in the left phase and y is even in the right phase, the next two-block tape is again of that kind or the tape becomes all ones. From 1^n A>0 the left phase restarts at E(3, n−2); the alternating block goes 3, 10, 24, 52, …, using 12, 26, 54, … ones, and the run halts if exactly one is left: n = 15, 41, 95, 205, 423, … (n = 28·2k − 2k − 13), and also n = 3 and 29 (checked for every n ≤ 400).

All-ones moments are rare: n = 4, 10, 58, 81, 278, 634 in the first 109 steps, and only 5881, 9702, 12113, 28074, 29561 and 405562 between 109 and 1015. None was in the list. A crude model (a phase change hits an exact value with chance about 1/width) makes such moments rarer and rarer, and each must also land on a list whose members double: the machine very probably never halts. A proof would have to control the exact remainders of a doubling map.
Its near-twins 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_0RA1LC_1RA1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE and 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_1RA1LC_0RB1LE_1RF0LD_---0RE share states B, D, E, F and the left phase, and behave the same way with their own fatal lists.

sections.heading: The phase map in Lean
html: Every configuration the run passes through at a phase boundary is one of three shapes: E(x, z) = E>0 (10)^x 1^z, A(x, y) = (10)^x 1^y A>0 and the bounce frame Q(m, j, t) = (10)^m 1 D>0 0 (1010)^j 1^t. The function next in lean/Phases.lean sends each one to the next shape the machine reaches, and next_sound proves each of its 25 cases for all parameters, from symbolic runs generated by py/pieces.py. Nothing is left out: next is undefined only at E(x, 0) and E(x, 1), and those halt.

So the question is exactly whether the orbit of A(0, 0) (the blank tape) under next reaches E(x, 0) or E(x, 1) (halts_iff). The first 108 iterates do not (native_decide); by the step counts that is about 4.1·1021 machine steps. The even phases cannot reach a halt without an all-ones tape in between, and for all-ones tapes shorter than 105 cells Lean checks which ones lead to a halt first: n = 3 or 28·2k − 2k − 13 (15, 41, 95, 205, …). The last open step is to prove that list for every n and to show that the run never hits it.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.333). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.343).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,094 cells (1,649 left of the start, 1,718 right), with a density of 1s of 0.746.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Two blocks, (10)^x and 1^y, take turns doubling at each other's expense; it halts only if an all-ones tape 1^n ever has n = 28·2^k − 2k − 13 (or 3, 29), and that has not happened.
